anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: All four facts moved from fails to holds, and Before held none of them, so nothing was lost. Before never offered reject, recommended deliver in A and assess in C, and used a multi-sentence recommendation in A. After puts reject first with a single conflict-only sentence and base citation in A and C, naming only the first conflict in A. In B it keeps deliver recommended, with reject third and no rejection rationale. Every reject row says nothing is written until a step is picked. In C the merge-restriction and no-repair sentences sit in their own paragraph before the recommendation, which keeps the sentence above Pick one conflict-only; keep the wording that forces that separation, since it is the only thing keeping the obstacle fact from failing. Two residual risks are worth tightening. First, C's reject row promises steps to "post it and close the PR" although the viewer cannot close, so consider wording the row consequence as "choose which posting or closing steps are available" so it does not over-promise under READ. Second, the pre-recommendation obstacle paragraph in C runs two sentences; cap it explicitly so it cannot grow into a second explanation or drift into the recommendation sentence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: All four facts move from fails to holds, and Before held none, so nothing was lost. Before never offered a reject row: it recommended deliver in A and assess in C, and folded the GitHub merge restriction into C's reason. After adds the reject row on every first menu and puts it first with the sole recommendation in A and C, where A's sentence names only the first conflict in report order (the catalog copy breaking the one-owner rule). In B it sits after deliver and assess, unrecommended and with no extra rejection rationale. Every reject row states a write-free consequence ("write nothing until a step is picked"). The thinnest margin is C: the two sentences on the merge restriction and unavailable deliver sit between the gate line and the recommendation. They pass only because they are a separate paragraph and the single sentence immediately above Pick one is conflict-only. To keep that stable, keep the wording that places merge-withhold and omission sentences before, never inside or after, the recommendation, and state that the recommendation sentence carries only the conflict and its base citation. Consider capping those preceding sentences or requiring the base citation (docs/architecture.md:21) in the reason so replies do not drift into explaining permissions. C's reason also paraphrases the remedy as "instead of respecting its public interface"; tell the model to name the conflict only, so a remedy clause does not grow into a second explanation of reject.
